newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money stays rooted in liquid mkt.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money stays rooted in liquid mkt.

text.p: Manila overnight money continued to stay rooted at its previous levels, a little above the Central Banks's borrowing rate of 10.50 percent, traders said.
The average rate was unchanged at 10.53125 percent, with the rates moving from 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent.
"The market's soft," a trader said, since banks have not been investing heavily in term reverse repos due to the new 20 percent tax.
The market had 20 lenders and 13 borrowers.
Traders said the market will have a net outflow of one billion pesos today but this will not affect the liquidity in the market.
"That's inconsequential," a foreign bank dealer said.
Banks are to make 4.0 billion pesos in payments for the two-year Treasury notes sold on Tuesday. At the same time, some 3.0 billion pesos of these notes will mature.
Despite the high liquidity, rates are not expected to go lower because this may trigger peso speculation, traders said.
In the secondary market for T-bills, sellers have emerged, a trader said.
"At these levels, the market is of the view that interest rates have bottomed out while Central bank keeps its bid and offer at 10.50 and 13.0 percent," he said.
Banks are adopting the strategy of restocking their inventory at the auction and just servicing their clients' needs.
A Reuter poll of eight institutions showed offer rates ranging from 10.65 to 10.75 percent for three-month bills; 10.95 to 11.075 for six months; and 11.30 to 11.375 for one year.
